title: CARF Accreditation for Behavioral Health Providers: Standards, Survey Process, Timeline and Cost (2026)
summary: How behavioral health and SUD programs earn and keep CARF accreditation in 2026: the standards manual sections, the survey steps, the four accreditation decisions, a realistic timeline, how the fee is calculated and a 9-month readiness plan.
body_markdown:
CARF accreditation is a peer-reviewed award from CARF International, an independent nonprofit, earned by showing surveyors that your program conforms to the Behavioral Health Standards Manual in effect on your survey date. The path runs from self-evaluation and a survey application to an on-site survey, a decision about six to eight weeks later, a Quality Improvement Plan within 90 days and an annual conformance report. Expect a year or more of preparation. CARF prices the survey by surveyor-days, not revenue.


This hub covers accreditation itself: the standards manual, the decisions, the survey, timeline, cost, where it's required and a 9-month readiness plan. For the record-level requirements surveyors check, see our guide to the[10 key CARF documentation requirements](https://blog.adentris.com/10-key-behavioral-health-carf-documentation-requirements-for-compliance/) , which this article links rather than repeats.


The short version


- CARF accreditation is voluntary, but SAMHSA certification of an opioid treatment program depends on accreditation by an approved body, and some states and payers require it.
- Every behavioral health survey applies Section 1 (ASPIRE to Excellence business practices) and Section 2 (general program standards). Core program and population standards depend on what you accredit.
- The decisions are Three-Year, One-Year, Provisional and Nonaccreditation, plus an Inaugural One-Year option for new organizations.
- CARF's own preparation plan starts 12 months out. Apply at least three months before your two-month survey window, expect the report six to eight weeks after the survey and file the QIP within 90 days.
- The survey fee is based on surveyors and days, plus travel and taxes. Staff time is the bigger line. CARF's ASAM Level of Care Certification has its own published fees.


## What CARF is, and what it accredits


CARF International was established in 1966 as an independent, nonprofit accreditor of health and human services, with headquarters in Tucson, Arizona. Its December 2025 brochure says the CARF family includes more than 64,000 accredited programs and services at over 30,000 locations on five continents. Behavioral Health is one of seven program areas, alongside a separate Opioid Treatment Program area, Medical Rehabilitation and four others.


CARF accredits programs, not whole companies. You pick the core programs that match what you deliver, such as Outpatient Treatment, Intensive Outpatient Treatment, Partial Hospitalization, Residential Treatment, Withdrawal Management or Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics, and add specialty designations where they fit. CARF lists two additions for 2026: a Sobering Center program and an Integrated Primary Care specialty designation.


Two things get confused with accreditation. A state license is the legal permission to operate, and CARF describes accreditation as a review with a wider scope than licensing or certification. ASAM Level of Care Certification, which CARF administers for adult residential levels 3.1, 3.5 and 3.7, is a separate credential with its own application and fees. For how level-of-care decisions hold up with payers, see our[ASAM level of care documentation guide](https://blog.adentris.com/asam-level-of-care-documentation-guide/) .


## How the Behavioral Health standards manual is organized


CARF publishes a new Behavioral Health Standards Manual every year, and each edition governs surveys from July 1 to June 30. The 2026 edition applies to surveys conducted between July 1, 2026 and June 30, 2027. It contains the accreditation policies and procedures, the standards, intent statements, a list of changes from the prior year and appendices for required written documentation and operational timelines. Start with those appendices.


The table uses section names from a public CARF report on a September 2025 survey under the 2025 manual. Codes shift between editions, so confirm them in your own copy.


Section What it covers Example subsections (2025 numbering)


**Section 1. ASPIRE to Excellence** Business practices for the whole organization 1.A Leadership, 1.G Risk Management, 1.H Health and Safety, 1.K Rights of Persons Served, 1.M Performance Measurement and Management, 1.N Performance Improvement


**Section 2. General Program Standards** How every accredited program handles a person from screening to discharge 2.A Program/Service Structure, 2.B Screening and Access to Services, 2.C Person-Centered Planning, 2.D Transition/Discharge, 2.E Medication Use, 2.F Promoting Nonviolent Practices, 2.G Records of the Persons Served, 2.H Quality Records Management, 2.I Service Delivery Using Information and Communication Technologies


**Section 3. Core Treatment Program Standards** One subsection per treatment program on your application 3.B Case Management/Services Coordination, 3.P Residential Treatment


**Section 4. Core Support Program Standards** Support programs 4.G Prevention


**Section 5. Specific Population Designation Standards** Added when you serve a designated population 5.C Children and Adolescents


**Supplements** Extra standards for certain structures Network standards for organizations that contract with participating providers


In plain terms, ASPIRE is how you run the business, Section 2 is how every program treats a person, and Sections 3 to 5 cover what's specific to the service and the population. The 2025 Delaware team split the same way: one administrative surveyor and two program surveyors.


## Accreditation outcomes and what each one requires


Decision What CARF says it means What comes next


**Three-Year Accreditation** Meets each Accreditation Condition and shows substantial conformance to the standards QIP within 90 days, then an Annual Conformance to Quality Report each year of the term


**One-Year Accreditation** Meets the Accreditation Conditions but has significant areas of deficiency, with evidence it can and will correct them QIP within 90 days. The next survey decides the next status


**Provisional Accreditation** Awarded when a One-Year term expires and the organization is still at that level. Lasts one year Must function at the Three-Year level at the next survey or receive Nonaccreditation


**Nonaccreditation** Major deficiencies in several areas, concerns about benefit, health, welfare or safety, or failure to meet an Accreditation Condition No accreditation. Reapply when ready


**Inaugural One-Year** (formerly Preliminary) For new organizations that show processes and systems before they serve people A full follow-up survey about six months after services begin


**Accreditation with stipulations** CARF may require ongoing reporting or other action toward conformance As stated in CARF's notice


For opioid treatment programs the decision has a second consequence. Under 42 CFR 8.11(a)(5), an OTP renewing SAMHSA certification with a one-year accreditation may receive a one-year conditional certification. If it doesn't reach standard accreditation within that year, the conditional certification lapses and the Attorney General is notified that the program's registration should be revoked.


Our advice is short. Treat a One-Year decision as an operating emergency, not a disappointment.


## The CARF survey process, step by step


1. **Preparation and self-evaluation.** Submit CARF's New Organization Questionnaire. You get a resource specialist, access to the Customer Connect portal and confirmation of which manual applies. CARF recommends a self-study, using its survey preparation workbook.
2. **Survey application and intent to survey.** The application names your programs, locations, leadership and a preferred two-month survey window. Submit it at least three months before that window. CARF invoices the survey fee and starts scheduling. Written notice of the dates arrives at least 30 days ahead.
3. **The on-site survey.** Surveyors are peers from the field, matched to your programs. They interview consenting current and former persons served, staff, leadership and stakeholders such as referral sources and payers, observe services and review policies, plans and records. Team size and length depend on scope. The Delaware survey covered several locations with three surveyors over three days.
4. **Decision and report.** About six to eight weeks after the survey you receive the decision letter and report, with strengths, recommendations tied to standard numbers and optional consultation. The certificate follows within 60 days of the decision.
5. **Quality Improvement Plan.** Within 90 days of the decision notice, submit a QIP that answers every recommendation with actions taken or planned. SAMHSA-certified OTPs also owe a SAMHSA Implementation Report within 180 days.
6. **Annual Conformance to Quality Report.** Each year, leadership signs an ACQR stating that the organization uses the current CARF standards. CARF sends the form about ten weeks before it's due.


Recommendations and consultation differ. A recommendation means a standard wasn't fully met and must go in your QIP. Consultation is advice you aren't required to address.


## How long CARF accreditation takes


When What happens


12 months before the survey Choose programs, contact CARF, form a committee, attend CARF 101 training, read the manual


9 months before Presurvey with the survey preparation workbook and an action plan


6 months before Submit the survey application, at least three months before the preferred window


1 to 2 months before Written notice of dates at least 30 days ahead, survey notice posted


Survey On site, with team size and days set by scope


6 to 8 weeks after Decision letter and report, certificate within 60 days of the decision


Within 90 days of the decision Quality Improvement Plan


Every year of the term Annual Conformance to Quality Report


Add it up and a new organization should expect roughly 12 to 15 months from first call to decision letter. A licensed program with policies and outcome data in place can compress preparation, but not the fixed lags. Three months of application lead time, a two-month survey window and six to eight weeks for the report put the floor at roughly four and a half to seven months between application and decision.


## What CARF accreditation costs in 2026


CARF doesn't price accreditation on revenue. Its brochure says the fee structure is based on the number of surveyors and days needed to complete the survey, plus applicable travel expenses and taxes, and CARF gives estimates on request. As of November 2026 we couldn't find a current per-surveyor-day rate published on carf.org, so we won't quote one. Figures in older trade articles are out of date.


The structure itself is arithmetic. A survey with three surveyors on site for three days is nine surveyor-days, billed at CARF's rate, plus travel. More programs or locations can mean more surveyors or more days.


Cost line Set by What drives it


**Survey fee** CARF Surveyors and days, based on the programs and locations in your application


**Travel and taxes** CARF invoice Locations and distance


**Standards manual and survey preparation workbook** CARF bookstore The edition for your survey year, in print or as a download


**Staff time** You Policy writing, plan updates, record review, drills, interview preparation


**Training and outside help** You CARF 101, consultants or a mock survey, all optional


**ASAM Level of Care Certification** (separate) CARF published schedule Base fee $4,540, or $3,520 for a facility with CARF-accredited services. $500 per additional level of care, $1,000 to reschedule. Applies to applications submitted by March 15, 2027 for survey timeframes from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027


I'd budget staff time as the largest line. The survey fee is fixed by scope, while the hours spent writing procedures and fixing records are not.


## Why accreditation matters: OTP certification, states and payers


### Opioid treatment programs: required by federal rule


Under 42 CFR 8.11(a)(2), an OTP can't obtain SAMHSA certification unless it holds current, valid accreditation from an Accreditation Body or other entity the Secretary designates. As of SAMHSA's page updated October 22, 2026, the approved bodies are CARF International, Social Current (previously the Council on Accreditation), The Joint Commission, the National Commission on Correctional Health Care and the Washington State Department of Health.


Certification lasts up to three years. A new OTP that has applied for accreditation can receive provisional certification for up to one year under 8.11(d), and accreditation bodies must survey OTPs at least every three years under 8.4(a)(1).


### State certification and licensure


Some states write accreditation into certification. Ohio's statute, R.C. 5119.36, has required applicants for initial certification of community behavioral health services to hold national accreditation since October 3, 2023, and renewal applicants since October 1, 2025. The director accepts The Joint Commission, CARF, the Council on Accreditation or another body the director considers appropriate, and certifies without further evaluation when the accreditation is current and appropriate. Other states vary widely, so read your own licensing rule.


### Payer networks and federal programs


- **Commercial.** In a June 24, 2024 notice, Blue Cross NC required CARF or Joint Commission accreditation, plus the right state license, for in-network PHP and IOP services, and for residential treatment unless the facility uses the state survey alternative.
- **TRICARE.** 32 CFR 199.6 requires residential treatment centers, PHPs, SUD rehabilitation facilities, IOPs and free-standing OTPs to hold accreditation from an approved organization. TRICARE participation agreements name The Joint Commission, CARF and the Council on Accreditation.
- **Youth residential.** Under 42 U.S.C. 672(k)(4)(G), a Qualified Residential Treatment Program must be licensed and accredited by CARF, The Joint Commission, the Council on Accreditation or another approved nonprofit accreditor.
- **CCBHCs.** CMS told states in October 2026 that they may rely on recognized accrediting organizations with CCBHC accreditation programs when certifying CCBHCs, and CARF lists CCBHC as a Behavioral Health core program.


## CARF vs Joint Commission, briefly


Most of the rules above accept either. Ohio's statute, Blue Cross NC's standards and SAMHSA's OTP list all name both. The practical differences sit in survey style and scope. CARF schedules your survey inside a two-month window you choose and says there are no surprise visits, while The Joint Commission surveys behavioral health organizations largely unannounced. CARF's standards center on person-centered planning and outcomes, Joint Commission's on patient safety across health care.


For the full comparison and how to choose, read our[CARF vs. Joint Commission guide](https://blog.adentris.com/comparing-behavioral-health-standards-carf-vs-joint-commission/) .


## Common survey findings and conformance gaps


We couldn't find a national list of most-cited behavioral health standards published by CARF, so the best evidence is public survey reports. One example: Delaware's Division of Prevention and Behavioral Health Services earned a Three-Year Accreditation after a September 2025 survey, and its report still lists recommendations worth checking against your own program.


Gap What the 2025 report found How to close it


**Analysis without an effectiveness check** 1.H.7.c.(5) and 1.H.11.b.(6): drill and critical incident analyses didn't address whether the actions taken accomplished the intended results. 1.K.4.b.(6): the same gap in complaint analysis Add a "did it work?" field to every drill, incident and complaint analysis, and fill it in


**Practice without a written procedure** 2.A.12: measurement-informed care was in use, with a user manual, but no written procedures naming tools, intervals, how results are shared and staff training Write down the procedure your staff already follow


**Assessment content gaps** 2.B.13.j: the assessment had no questions on complementary health approaches Map your assessment form to every element of the screening and assessment standards


**Missed timed requirements** 2.F.9.a: debriefing after seclusion or restraint must start within 24 hours, with no formal process when the therapist was unavailable Track timed requirements as deadlines, each with an owner and a backup


None of these were about the quality of care. They were about proof that the organization checks its own work. At the record level the typical gaps are plans that aren't individualized and reviews that run late, and our[10 CARF documentation examples](https://blog.adentris.com/10-essential-behavioral-health-carf-documentation-examples-for-compliance/) show what conforming entries look like.


## A 9-month CARF readiness plan


CARF's own guide starts 12 months out. If you're licensed and your policies are current, nine months is realistic. This is the sequence I'd use.


Months before survey Focus Deliverables


9 Scope and team Programs and locations chosen, manual confirmed with your resource specialist, committee named, CARF 101 attended


8 Gap analysis Presurvey with the survey preparation workbook, gap list with owners and due dates


7 Written documents Every plan, policy and analysis in the manual's required written documentation appendix drafted or updated


6 Application Survey application submitted in Customer Connect, at least three months before your preferred window


5 Records Quarterly professional review of current and closed records running, findings logged and corrected


4 Safety and rights Unannounced emergency drills analyzed, incident and complaint analyses include effectiveness checks, rights and grievance materials current


3 Mock survey Internal or outside mock survey, staff and persons served briefed on interviews, outcome data summarized


2 Close gaps Gap list closed or documented, written notice of dates received, survey notice poster displayed


1 Logistics Survey room, document set, updated organization chart with names and titles, interview schedule


After Follow-through QIP submitted within 90 days of the decision, ACQR dates on the compliance calendar


## Records and documentation readiness


Surveyors review records of current and former persons served, and Section 2 sets the rules they read them against. In the 2025 numbering, 2.G covers confidentiality, timeframes for entries, individual record requirements and duplicate records. 2.H requires a quarterly professional review of current and closed records, with the findings used to improve services.


That quarterly review is where most programs are thinnest. A handful of charts shows patterns, but it can't tell you whether the plan review due last week happened on every open chart. We compare the two approaches in our guide to[full chart sweeps vs sampling](https://blog.adentris.com/chart-audit-sud-full-sweep-vs-sampling/) .


For record content, from person-centered assessment to discharge planning, use the[10 key CARF documentation requirements](https://blog.adentris.com/10-key-behavioral-health-carf-documentation-requirements-for-compliance/) . To build those into EHR forms, see the[9 elements of a CARF documentation template](https://blog.adentris.com/9-key-elements-of-a-behavioral-health-carf-documentation-contract-template/) .

## Frequently asked questions


**What is CARF accreditation?**


CARF accreditation is a peer-reviewed quality award from CARF International, an independent nonprofit accreditor founded in 1966. A program earns it by showing on-site surveyors that it conforms to the standards manual for its survey year, then keeps it with a Quality Improvement Plan and annual conformance reports.


**How long does CARF accreditation take?**


CARF's preparation guide starts 12 months before the survey. Submit the application at least three months before your preferred two-month window, expect the decision six to eight weeks after the survey, and file the QIP within 90 days of the decision. A new organization should plan on roughly 12 to 15 months from first contact to decision.


**How much does CARF accreditation cost?**


CARF bases the survey fee on the number of surveyors and days needed, plus travel and taxes, not on revenue, and gives an estimate on request. We couldn't verify a published per-day rate as of November 2026. Staff time for preparation is usually the larger cost.


**How long does CARF accreditation last?**


A Three-Year Accreditation lasts three years, with an Annual Conformance to Quality Report each year. A One-Year Accreditation signals significant deficiencies. A Provisional Accreditation lasts one year, and the organization must reach the Three-Year level at its next survey or receive Nonaccreditation.


**Is CARF accreditation required?**


Not everywhere. Opioid treatment programs need accreditation from a SAMHSA-approved body, such as CARF or The Joint Commission, to hold SAMHSA certification under 42 CFR 8.11. Some states, Ohio among them, require national accreditation for certification, and some payers require it for residential, PHP and IOP networks.


**Is ASAM Level of Care Certification the same as CARF accreditation?**


No. CARF administers ASAM Level of Care Certification for adult residential levels 3.1, 3.5 and 3.7 as a separate credential with its own application and fees. Accreditation reviews the whole program against CARF's standards. A program can hold either one or both.
